key_insight: Directly optimizing pass@k selects partial solutions to maximize the chance of at least one correct completion, naturally balancing quality and diversity.
engineering_relevance: Pruning candidates after short prefixes can focus inference compute on a promising, nonredundant pool rather than completing every reasoning path.
method: Generate short prefixes for multiple candidate solutions.
Select a pool by optimizing its probability of yielding at least one correct completion.
Continue only retained candidates, rewarding quality while penalizing redundancy.
evidence_signal: Across eight open-weight reasoning models, the method outperforms quality-based and diversity-based pruning baselines, with especially pronounced gains at moderate retained-pool sizes.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify selection overhead or explain how pool-level success probabilities are estimated, leaving practical compute savings uncertain.
paper_title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
